review_basis: Visually inspected all 29 original public/course-visuals/aif-course/module-08 numbered WebP images individually in order. Narration rewritten following exact diagram arrows, visible text/examples, numeric values, callouts, and exam comparisons, with product lifecycle caveats.

scenes.title: Amazon Lex
scenes.narration: The top row shows an end-to-end hotel-booking chatbot. A customer says Book a hotel room. Amazon Lex recognizes the intent BookHotel and asks for missing slots, including city and check-in date. The lower conversation bubbles show the user responding Seattle and April 12. Once all required information has been gathered, Lex invokes a configured AWS Lambda fulfillment function. Lambda calls the hotel's backend, checks availability, creates the booking only when authorized, and returns a confirmation to Lex. The green result box shows a sample confirmation for Seattle on April 12 with number HTL12345. The bottom-right exam summary separates the roles: Lex manages intent and slots, whereas Lambda or application code performs the actual reservation. Amazon Transcribe only changes speech into text and cannot make a booking by itself. In real systems, authorization, availability and confirmation are essential safeguards.

scenes.title: Amazon Personalize
scenes.narration: Start at the upper-left data sources panel. Amazon S3 holds historical views, clicks and purchases plus item metadata, while a fresh-events stream adds recent user activity through a supported events API. The arrows enter Amazon Personalize, which uses an appropriate recommendation recipe and model to learn user and item relationships. A retail application calls GetRecommendations with relevant user or session context and receives a ranked list to display. The worked GardenMart example below follows a customer browsing trowels, pruners and rakes, then shows related gardening products such as plant food, a pot, gloves and a hose. The right-hand notes distinguish recommendations from ordinary keyword search: the former use interaction patterns and relationships, whereas search matches a requested query or filter. This system predicts item rankings; it does not produce free-form product descriptions by itself. Verify freshness, permissions and recommendation quality using real interaction data.

scenes.title: Amazon Personalize – Recipes
scenes.narration: Read across the top: the application requests personalized results, a selected Amazon Personalize recipe trains a solution version, and a compatible real-time solution is deployed as a campaign. The application then invokes GetRecommendations or GetPersonalizedRanking with a campaign ARN and receives recommended or reordered items. In the lower-left decision table, User-Personalization-v2 recommends items for a user, Personalized-Ranking-v2 reorders an existing list, Trending-Now surfaces currently popular items, and Similar-Items finds related products. The smaller row also names Popularity-Count, Next-Best-Action and Item-Affinity for different tasks. The bottom-right architecture focuses specifically on re-ranking an existing product shelf: the application supplies candidates, the ranking recipe orders them, and the result is a personalized list. Avoid assuming all these recipes use the same deployment and invocation APIs; action recommendation and segmentation have different operations. Choose by task and supported data.
